questions.question: Your child sent you a strange link on WhatsApp saying 'Open it quickly!' What should you do?
questions.context: Suspicious links can steal your data or compromise your device.

options.text: Enter my personal details on the page to view the content
options.rationale: ❌ Any site asking for personal data without a clear reason may be a scam.

options.text: Forward it to everyone to see what is inside
options.rationale: ❌ Forwarding a suspicious link puts others at risk too.

options.text: Do not open it until I verify it comes from a trusted source
options.rationale: ✅ Verifying before opening protects your data and device.

options.text: Open it right away because my child sent it
options.rationale: ❌ Even family accounts can be compromised. Ask your child before opening.

questions.question: How can you tell if a new app you are about to download is safe?
questions.context: Some apps steal your data or cause problems on your device.

options.text: Download it from the official store and read the reviews
options.rationale: ✅ Using the official store and checking reviews reduces risk.

options.text: Grant every permission it asks for
options.rationale: ❌ You should deny unnecessary permissions like camera or contacts access.

options.text: Download it from any website on the internet
options.rationale: ❌ APK files from random websites may contain malware.

options.text: Download it just because friends mentioned it
options.rationale: ❌ Friends' recommendations are not proof of security.

questions.question: A website asks you to register with your full name, phone number, and home address. How do you respond?
questions.context: Personal data is valuable and should not be shared everywhere.

options.text: Delete all accounts from my device
options.rationale: ❌ Not every site is dangerous, but caution is essential.

options.text: Enter fake information as a joke
options.rationale: ❌ Entering random data is not a real solution; deciding mindfully is better.

options.text: Fill in all the details just to finish quickly
options.rationale: ❌ Excess personal information can be leaked or sold.

options.text: Ask first: Is this site trustworthy, and does it really need all this info?
options.rationale: ✅ Pausing to think before sharing protects your privacy.

questions.question: Someone calls claiming to be from your bank and asks for your card number and PIN. What do you do?
questions.context: Real banks never ask for your PIN or password.

options.text: Share no information and call the bank back using their official number
options.rationale: ✅ Verifying through the official channel keeps you safe.

options.text: Give them the PIN so they can fix the issue
options.rationale: ❌ Any request for your PIN is almost certainly a scam.

options.text: Ask the caller to send a photo of their ID card
options.rationale: ❌ ID photos can easily be faked.

options.text: Provide the details so my account does not get closed
options.rationale: ❌ Threats of immediate account closure are a common scam tactic.

questions.question: You discover a private photo of your child posted on a public page. What is the first thing you should do?
questions.context: Children's photos require special protection online.

options.text: Stay silent and do nothing
options.rationale: ❌ Silence does not help; protecting your child's privacy is a right.

options.text: Report the photo and request its immediate removal
options.rationale: ✅ Prompt reporting helps remove harmful or unauthorized content.

options.text: Share the post so everyone knows about it
options.rationale: ❌ Spreading the photo further harms the child's privacy.

options.text: Like the photo to avoid upsetting anyone
options.rationale: ❌ Engaging with the post can boost its visibility.

questions.question: Your device has become unusually slow and strange pop-ups keep appearing. What could this mean?
questions.context: These symptoms can be a sign of malware or a virus.

options.text: It might be malware — I should run a security scan right away
options.rationale: ✅ Regular security checks help catch problems early.

options.text: Remove the battery and put it back in
options.rationale: ❌ That is only a temporary reset and will not fix a software infection.

options.text: Keep using the device as normal
options.rationale: ❌ Ignoring symptoms can allow malware to steal your data.

options.text: Download any random 'speed booster' from the internet
options.rationale: ❌ Untrusted utilities often make the problem worse.

questions.question: What is the difference between a strong password and a weak password?
questions.context: Weak passwords make it easy for attackers to access your accounts.

options.text: You should use the exact same password for every account
options.rationale: ❌ If one account is breached, all your other accounts become vulnerable.

options.text: A password like '123456' is fine if it is easy to remember
options.rationale: ❌ Common passwords can be cracked in seconds.

options.text: Passwords do not matter as long as I do not download apps
options.rationale: ❌ Strong passwords matter even for everyday browsing and email.

options.text: A strong one combines letters, numbers, and symbols and avoids names or birthdays
options.rationale: ✅ Length and variety make passwords much harder to guess.

questions.question: You are connected to public Wi-Fi at a café or airport. What should you avoid doing?
questions.context: Public Wi-Fi networks are often unsecured.

options.text: Avoid online banking or entering sensitive personal data
options.rationale: ✅ Sensitive transactions should wait for a trusted connection.

options.text: Use it for everything just like my home network
options.rationale: ❌ Public networks can be intercepted by attackers.

options.text: Download apps from links posted around the café
options.rationale: ❌ Public QR codes or links can easily be spoofed.

options.text: Leave my unlocked device on the table
options.rationale: ❌ Physical theft or unauthorized access is also a major risk.

questions.question: Your child wants to livestream or post a public video of themselves. How should you handle it?
questions.context: Public posts stay online and can reach strangers with bad intentions.

options.text: Let them stream publicly and just watch from afar
options.rationale: ❌ Watching from afar cannot undo public exposure.

options.text: Discuss the risks together and keep sharing private or family-only
options.rationale: ✅ Open dialogue and clear boundaries protect your child long-term.

options.text: Let them post whatever they want publicly
options.rationale: ❌ Children often do not realize the long-term risks of public sharing.

options.text: Ban them from using the internet completely
options.rationale: ❌ A total ban is unrealistic; guided use teaches safer habits.

questions.question: You receive an email saying 'You won a prize!' and asking for your personal details. What do you do?
questions.context: Fake prize notifications are among the most common online scams.

options.text: Treat the email as suspicious and do not enter any information
options.rationale: ✅ Healthy skepticism is the first step to staying safe.

options.text: Forward the email to the whole family
options.rationale: ❌ Sharing suspicious links puts family members at risk.

options.text: Reply to the email asking if it is real
options.rationale: ❌ Replying confirms to scammers that your email address is active.

options.text: Enter my details just in case I really won
options.rationale: ❌ Legitimate prizes do not demand sensitive data via unsolicited emails.

questions.question: What does a 'software update' do, and why is it important?
questions.context: Updates are not just about new features; they often patch security vulnerabilities.

options.text: It only changes colors and icons, so it is not important
options.rationale: ❌ Security fixes are a primary reason for many updates.

options.text: It fixes security gaps and strengthens device protection
options.rationale: ✅ Regular updates are a vital line of defense.

options.text: It slows down the device, so we should skip it
options.rationale: ❌ Skipping updates leaves your device exposed to known exploits.

options.text: We should only update when the device freezes
options.rationale: ❌ Waiting until something breaks is often too late.

questions.question: Someone on social media asks for a private photo or video. How should you respond?
questions.context: People online may not be who they claim to be.

options.text: Report them, but still send the photo anyway
options.rationale: ❌ Reporting does not undo the risk of sending private content.

options.text: Send an old photo since it will not matter
options.rationale: ❌ Any personal photo can be misused.

options.text: Send it because they seem polite and friendly
options.rationale: ❌ Politeness online is no guarantee of honesty or safety.

options.text: Never send private content to anyone I do not know and trust in real life
options.rationale: ✅ Digital boundaries are an essential part of personal safety.

questions.question: What is 'Phishing'?
questions.context: Understanding security terms helps you spot scams.

options.text: An attempt to trick you into entering your data on a fake website or message
options.rationale: ✅ That is the exact definition of phishing.

options.text: A type of fishing video game
options.rationale: ❌ The word sounds similar, but it is a cybersecurity threat.

options.text: A method for repairing broken devices
options.rationale: ❌ Phishing is fraud, not device maintenance.

options.text: A program that speeds up your internet connection
options.rationale: ❌ That is misleading; phishing is an online scam.

questions.question: In an online game, a player asks your child to meet up in person outside the game. What should your child do?
questions.context: Online games can be used by strangers to initiate unsafe contact.

options.text: Give them a personal social media account instead
options.rationale: ❌ Sharing personal accounts opens the door to further unsafe contact.

options.text: Meet them because they seem nice in the game
options.rationale: ❌ Friendly behavior online can be a disguise.

options.text: Say 'No' and tell a parent right away
options.rationale: ✅ Refusing offline meetups and telling a parent keeps the child safe.

options.text: Keep quiet and not tell anyone
options.rationale: ❌ Secrecy leaves the child vulnerable.

questions.question: How do you best protect your online accounts from being hacked?
questions.context: Multiple layers of protection are much stronger than a single one.

options.text: Skip updates so the device stays fast
options.rationale: ❌ Updates are essential for closing security holes.

options.text: Use a strong password + enable two-factor authentication + keep software updated
options.rationale: ✅ Layered security drastically reduces the chance of a breach.

options.text: Stay logged in on shared devices so I do not forget my password
options.rationale: ❌ Leaving accounts open on shared or unlocked devices is risky.

options.text: Use one strong password across all accounts
options.rationale: ❌ If that single password leaks, every account is at risk.

questions.question: An app or website asks to turn on 'Location Services' before you use it. What do you do?
questions.context: Many apps request location data without genuinely needing it.

options.text: Never use maps or any location feature ever
options.rationale: ❌ Some apps genuinely need location; the key is selective permission.

options.text: Always allow location access for every app
options.rationale: ❌ Constant location tracking exposes your daily movements.

options.text: Allow it only if the app truly needs it to function (like a maps app)
options.rationale: ✅ Location sharing should always be justified and limited.

options.text: Set every app to 'While Using' without checking if it needs location
options.rationale: ❌ Even 'While Using' is unnecessary if the app has no reason to know where you are.

questions.question: Your child mentions that someone online told them to keep secrets from Mom and Dad. What should you do?
questions.context: Online predators often try to isolate a child from their parents.

options.text: Start an angry argument in the chat before blocking
options.rationale: ❌ Engaging fuels conflict; blocking, documenting, and reporting is safer.

options.text: Say nothing so my child does not feel embarrassed
options.rationale: ❌ Silence allows the unsafe contact to continue.

options.text: Tell my child they are overreacting
options.rationale: ❌ Dismissing their concern may stop them from speaking up next time.

options.text: Listen calmly, reassure my child, block/report the person, and stop contact
options.rationale: ✅ Calm listening and swift action protect your child and keep trust open.

questions.question: What should you do if your social media account gets hacked?
questions.context: How quickly you respond determines how much damage is done.

options.text: Change the password immediately, enable 2FA, and warn friends not to click strange links
options.rationale: ✅ These steps contain the damage and secure the account.

options.text: Wait a few days to see if the problem goes away on its own
options.rationale: ❌ Waiting gives the attacker more time to cause harm.

options.text: Reuse the same old password on a new account
options.rationale: ❌ Once a password is compromised, it is never safe to reuse.

options.text: Create a new account and ignore the hacked one
options.rationale: ❌ The compromised account can still be used to scam your contacts.

questions.question: How can you tell a genuine app apart from a fake look-alike?
questions.context: Fake apps often imitate popular ones to trick users.

options.text: If the icon looks similar to the original, it is fine
options.rationale: ❌ Icons and screenshots are easy to copy.

options.text: Download it whenever it is free or cheap
options.rationale: ❌ Free look-alikes are a common trap.

options.text: Check the developer name, download count, reviews, and requested permissions
options.rationale: ✅ Reviewing app details helps you spot imitations.

options.text: Ask random strangers in comments
options.rationale: ❌ Verifying official store details is much more reliable.

questions.question: Your child downloads a simple puzzle game that asks for camera and microphone access. What do you do?
questions.context: Some games collect far more data than they need.

options.text: Ask whether the game truly needs the camera or mic — if not, deny permission
options.rationale: ✅ Permissions should only be granted when genuinely needed.

options.text: Allow all permissions so the child can play right away
options.rationale: ❌ Unjustified permissions put your family's privacy at risk.

options.text: Delete the game without explaining why
options.rationale: ❌ Explaining the reason helps your child learn digital safety.

options.text: Ban games forever
options.rationale: ❌ A total ban does not teach how to evaluate permissions.

questions.question: Why is backing up your data important?
questions.context: Devices can be lost, broken, or compromised at any time.

options.text: Backups are only for banking apps
options.rationale: ❌ Personal photos, contacts, and documents need protection too.

options.text: It protects important photos and files if the device is lost or damaged
options.rationale: ✅ Regular backups ensure you do not lose family memories and important documents.

options.text: You only need to back up once when buying the phone
options.rationale: ❌ Ongoing backups are needed to keep recent data safe.

options.text: It slows down the device, so it is unnecessary
options.rationale: ❌ Losing all your files is far worse than a brief background sync.

questions.question: You find a harsh, bullying comment on your child's post. What is your first step?
questions.context: Cruel comments can deeply affect a child's emotional well-being.

options.text: Scold my child for receiving the comment
options.rationale: ❌ Blaming the victim is unfair; the bully is at fault.

options.text: Leave the comment up and ignore how my child feels
options.rationale: ❌ Ignoring cyberbullying leaves your child feeling unsupported.

options.text: Report/block the comment and comfort and support my child
options.rationale: ✅ Supporting your child emotionally and using platform reporting tools comes first.

options.text: Reply with insults of my own
options.rationale: ❌ Retaliating with insults usually escalates the conflict.

questions.question: What should you do if your child's phone or tablet is stolen?
questions.context: A stolen device exposes logged-in accounts and personal data.

options.text: Buy a new device and leave all old passwords unchanged
options.rationale: ❌ Old sessions on the stolen device could still access your accounts.

options.text: Change account passwords immediately, use remote locate/lock if available, and report it
options.rationale: ✅ Changing passwords and locking the device remotely protects your accounts.

options.text: Just wait and hope someone brings it back
options.rationale: ❌ Waiting gives whoever has the device time to access accounts.

options.text: Expect the child to handle the security steps alone
options.rationale: ❌ Children need adult help to secure accounts after a theft.

questions.question: How should you teach your child to handle upsetting content they accidentally see online?
questions.context: Children may stumble upon inappropriate content even with filters in place.

options.text: Tell them never to mention it to anyone
options.rationale: ❌ Your child needs to know you are a safe person to talk to.

options.text: Take away all devices immediately whenever they tell me
options.rationale: ❌ Punishing honesty makes children hide things next time.

options.text: Teach them to close the screen and come talk to me calmly about what they saw
options.rationale: ✅ Open, blame-free conversation builds lasting digital safety.

options.text: Leave them to figure it out on their own
options.rationale: ❌ Children need guidance to process confusing content.

questions.question: What should you avoid posting publicly about your child on social media?
questions.context: Oversharing details can put a child's safety and future privacy at risk.

options.text: Nothing — it is fine to share everything since they are my child
options.rationale: ❌ Oversharing can expose children to privacy and safety risks.

options.text: Only avoid blurry photos
options.rationale: ❌ Even high-quality photos can reveal sensitive location or school details.

options.text: Share every milestone publicly with the whole internet
options.rationale: ❌ Milestones can be celebrated safely with close family rather than the public.

options.text: Their school name/location, daily routine details, bath photos, and sensitive info
options.rationale: ✅ Keeping identifying and private details offline protects your child.

questions.question: Your child asks: 'What is a VPN?' What is the accurate answer?
questions.context: A reputable VPN encrypts traffic, though not every free VPN app is trustworthy.

options.text: A program that always makes your internet twice as fast
options.rationale: ❌ A VPN does not necessarily speed up connections; sometimes it slows them slightly.

options.text: A tool that encrypts your internet connection and helps hide your IP location
options.rationale: ✅ That is the core function of a VPN.

options.text: A piece of hardware that connects your phone directly to a satellite
options.rationale: ❌ A VPN is software encryption over your existing internet connection.

options.text: A tool that makes all paid websites free
options.rationale: ❌ That is a misconception.

questions.question: How do you set healthy screen-time boundaries for your child?
questions.context: Excessive screen time affects sleep, eyesight, and focus.

options.text: Only use screen limits as a punishment when you are angry
options.rationale: ❌ Healthy screen habits should be a normal daily routine, not just a punishment.

options.text: Let them use screens right up until they fall asleep
options.rationale: ❌ Screens right before bed disrupt sleep quality.

options.text: Set a clear daily limit suited to their age and encourage regular breaks
options.rationale: ✅ Clear, consistent boundaries reduce conflict and protect well-being.

options.text: Have no rules at all until an argument starts
options.rationale: ❌ Agreed-upon limits work much better than sudden arguments.

questions.question: What is the first thing you should do if you learn your personal data was part of a breach?
questions.context: Data breaches happen frequently and require prompt action.

options.text: Abandon every account I own and start over
options.rationale: ❌ Securing your existing accounts with new passwords and 2FA is usually sufficient.

options.text: Just complain online without changing my password
options.rationale: ❌ Venting does not secure your accounts.

options.text: Ignore it because breaches happen to everyone
options.rationale: ❌ Ignoring a breach leaves your accounts easy to take over.

options.text: Change my passwords immediately, enable 2FA, and monitor my accounts
options.rationale: ✅ Acting quickly prevents attackers from using leaked credentials.

questions.question: Why is it important to teach children never to share their live location online?
questions.context: Live location reveals where a child physically is in real time.

options.text: It does not matter as long as they are with friends
options.rationale: ❌ Public location sharing is risky even when with friends.

options.text: Because strangers could find out where the child lives, studies, or hangs out
options.rationale: ✅ Real-time location is highly sensitive safety information.

options.text: To save storage space on the device
options.rationale: ❌ Location sharing is a safety issue, not a storage issue.

options.text: So they do not spend too much time on the phone
options.rationale: ❌ That is about screen time, not location safety.

questions.question: What is Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
questions.context: Adding a second verification step significantly boosts account safety.

options.text: Typing your password twice on the same screen
options.rationale: ❌ Typing the same password twice is not two-factor authentication.

options.text: Changing your password twice every day
options.rationale: ❌ 2FA is a second login factor, not daily password changes.

options.text: Requiring a second verification code in addition to your password when signing in
options.rationale: ✅ 2FA adds an essential extra layer of protection.

options.text: Sharing your password with two family members
options.rationale: ❌ 2FA uses a second verification method, not password sharing.

questions.question: Your child is installing a simple game that asks for 'Access to Contacts'. How should you respond?
questions.context: Your contacts list contains private details of family and friends.

options.text: Take the device away permanently
options.rationale: ❌ Teaching how to manage permissions is more effective than a ban.

options.text: Delete the app silently without explaining why
options.rationale: ❌ Explaining the reason helps your child build good judgment.

options.text: Allow it so the app runs smoothly
options.rationale: ❌ Unnecessary access exposes your family's and friends' contact info.

options.text: Deny contacts access if the game does not need it, and check if the app is trustworthy
options.rationale: ✅ Permissions should only be granted when clearly necessary.

questions.question: What should you do if your child comes across a violent video on YouTube?
questions.context: Children can accidentally encounter content that is too intense for their age.

options.text: Turn off the video, talk calmly with my child about what they saw, and adjust filters
options.rationale: ✅ Calm conversation and better boundaries help your child process and stay safe.

options.text: Ignore it completely
options.rationale: ❌ Children need reassurance and guidance after seeing disturbing content.

options.text: Yell at the child for seeing the video
options.rationale: ❌ Yelling makes children afraid to tell you next time.

options.text: Let them keep watching so they 'learn about the real world'
options.rationale: ❌ Violent content can cause anxiety and distress in children.

questions.question: How do you distinguish an official app store listing from a fake one?
questions.context: Fake listings try to trick users into installing malicious software.

options.text: Trust it if the colors look similar to the original
options.rationale: ❌ Visual appearance is easy to imitate.

options.text: Verify the publisher name, review history, download count, and update track record
options.rationale: ✅ Checking publisher authenticity is the most reliable step.

options.text: Trust it if a link came in a random group chat
options.rationale: ❌ Always verify directly in the official app store.

options.text: Trust it if it promises lots of free rewards
options.rationale: ❌ 'Too good to be true' freebies are often bait.

questions.question: What should you do if intrusive pop-up ads suddenly start appearing all over your phone?
questions.context: Constant pop-up ads are often caused by adware or a shady app.

options.text: Run a security check and uninstall recently added or suspicious apps
options.rationale: ✅ Removing the offending app and scanning the device solves the root cause.

options.text: Tap the ads to see what they are offering
options.rationale: ❌ Tapping suspicious pop-ups can install more malware.

options.text: Wait and hope the pop-ups stop on their own
options.rationale: ❌ Delaying action leaves your device at risk.

options.text: Just restart the phone and do nothing else
options.rationale: ❌ Restarting will not remove an installed adware app.

questions.question: Why is it smart to hide notification previews on your lock screen?
questions.context: Lock-screen notifications can display private messages and verification codes to anyone nearby.

options.text: Only to make the wallpaper look prettier
options.rationale: ❌ Aesthetics are secondary; protecting private messages and OTP codes is the real benefit.

options.text: So private messages and login codes are not visible to anyone who picks up the phone
options.rationale: ✅ Good privacy starts with everyday habits.

options.text: It has no benefit at all
options.rationale: ❌ Every layer of privacy helps protect your accounts.

options.text: Because it doubles battery life
options.rationale: ❌ The battery impact is minimal; privacy is the main reason.

questions.question: Your child receives a threatening or blackmail message online. What is the very first step?
questions.context: Online extortion is a serious offense that requires calm, decisive action.

options.text: Keep silent out of embarrassment
options.rationale: ❌ Silence gives the blackmailer power.

options.text: Pay what they ask so they delete the content
options.rationale: ❌ Paying almost always leads to more demands.

options.text: Reassure my child, save evidence, do not pay or negotiate, and report it immediately
options.rationale: ✅ Supporting your child and reporting to the platform/authorities is the right response.

options.text: Focus only on blaming and punishing the child
options.rationale: ❌ Blaming the child increases fear and hides the problem.

questions.question: What should you do if you learn an app on your phone secretly harvests data in the background?
questions.context: Some apps abuse permissions to collect personal data.

options.text: Uninstall the app immediately, review permissions, and run a security scan
options.rationale: ✅ Removing the app and checking your device stops further data collection.

options.text: Keep using it as long as I do not type my name
options.rationale: ❌ Malicious apps can still access device data and identifiers.

options.text: Just open the app less often
options.rationale: ❌ Background apps can collect data even when you do not open them.

options.text: Keep it installed since I am not 100% sure
options.rationale: ❌ When an app is credibly flagged as unsafe, removing it is the safest choice.

questions.question: How do you teach your child to tell real news apart from fake news online?
questions.context: Misinformation spreads rapidly on social platforms.

options.text: If it has a dramatic photo, it must be true
options.rationale: ❌ Photos can be taken out of context or edited.

options.text: Read the headline only
options.rationale: ❌ Clickbait headlines are often misleading.

options.text: If thousands of people shared it, it must be real
options.rationale: ❌ Viral spread is not proof of accuracy.

options.text: Check the source, date, and evidence — and verify with trusted outlets before believing or sharing
options.rationale: ✅ Fact-checking sources is an essential digital literacy skill.

questions.question: What is the most important rule for passwords on critical accounts like email and banking?
questions.context: Core accounts like email and banking need the strongest protection.

options.text: Make each password long, unique, and never reused anywhere else
options.rationale: ✅ Unique, long passwords prevent a breach on one site from compromising others.

options.text: Keep it short and simple so it is easy to type
options.rationale: ❌ Short, simple passwords are easy to crack.

options.text: Use the same password for all accounts
options.rationale: ❌ Reusing passwords puts every account at risk if one leaks.

options.text: Tape the password onto the back of the phone
options.rationale: ❌ Anyone who picks up the phone would have full access.

questions.question: Why is it important to teach children to speak up about any strange online contact?
questions.context: Early reporting prevents online risks from escalating.

options.text: To make children afraid of technology
options.rationale: ❌ The goal is confident awareness, not fear.

options.text: Just to spy on everything the child does
options.rationale: ❌ The goal is safety and trust, not surveillance.

options.text: It is not necessary unless something bad has already happened
options.rationale: ❌ Catching red flags early prevents harm before it happens.

options.text: Because secrecy helps bad actors, while speaking up early lets parents protect the child
options.rationale: ✅ Open communication is the strongest first line of defense.

questions.question: Your child wants to create an account on a new social platform. What should you do first?
questions.context: Each platform has age ratings, privacy settings, and different risks.

options.text: Refuse to discuss technology at all
options.rationale: ❌ Guided conversation works better than avoidance.

options.text: Enter a fake adult birth year so they bypass age checks
options.rationale: ❌ Falsifying age removes child-safety protections on the platform.

options.text: Check the minimum age requirement, review privacy settings, and agree on family rules
options.rationale: ✅ Checking age appropriateness and privacy settings upfront keeps your child safer.

options.text: Let them sign up immediately without checking what the app is
options.rationale: ❌ Age-inappropriate platforms can expose children to harmful content and strangers.

questions.question: What should you do if false rumors or defamatory posts are shared about your family online?
questions.context: Online rumors can harm reputation and emotional well-being.

options.text: Post angry insults back at everyone in the comments
options.rationale: ❌ Public fights amplify the post and worsen the situation.

options.text: Make up false rumors about the other person in return
options.rationale: ❌ Retaliating with falsehoods creates ethical and legal problems.

options.text: Do nothing because platforms never remove anything
options.rationale: ❌ Platforms have reporting channels specifically for harassment and defamation.

options.text: Document evidence (screenshots), report to the platform, and seek official/legal help if needed
options.rationale: ✅ Calm, documented action protects your rights effectively.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of family photos being misused by AI manipulation (deepfakes)?
questions.context: AI tools can manipulate publicly available photos.

options.text: Post as many public photos as possible so people know the originals
options.rationale: ❌ Posting more public photos gives AI tools more material to misuse.

options.text: Limit public photos of children, keep accounts private to trusted people, and stay vigilant
options.rationale: ✅ Prevention and strong privacy settings reduce exposure.

options.text: Rely on a color filter to protect the photo
options.rationale: ❌ Simple filters do not stop image misuse.

options.text: Do not worry because deepfakes only target celebrities
options.rationale: ❌ Anyone's public photos can be misused.

questions.question: How should you explain 'cybercrime' when your child asks about it?
questions.context: Explaining digital concepts simply helps children build sound judgment.

options.text: Tell them it is an adult topic and refuse to explain
options.rationale: ❌ Age-appropriate explanations help children protect themselves.

options.text: Make up a random answer just to end the conversation
options.rationale: ❌ Inaccurate information leaves children confused.

options.text: Explain that harmful or illegal acts online are real offenses with real-world consequences
options.rationale: ✅ Connecting online actions to real-world ethics and laws helps children understand.

options.text: Scare them into thinking the computer itself is dangerous
options.rationale: ❌ Fear is not a substitute for understanding.

questions.question: What does 'safe browsing' really mean?
questions.context: Safe browsing is a combination of everyday habits.

options.text: Never using the internet at all
options.rationale: ❌ The internet is a useful tool when used safely.

options.text: Installing an antivirus app and then clicking any link freely
options.rationale: ❌ No tool can replace careful user habits.

options.text: Browsing as fast as possible
options.rationale: ❌ Speed has nothing to do with safety.

options.text: Using trusted sites, protecting personal data, and keeping security updates current
options.rationale: ✅ Safe browsing is a set of consistent, mindful habits.

questions.question: How do you keep your whole family comprehensively safe online?
questions.context: Family digital safety combines clear rules, open communication, and technical safeguards.

options.text: Ban children from ever touching technology
options.rationale: ❌ Guided learning prepares children better than total isolation.

options.text: Combine clear rules, open conversation, healthy screen boundaries, and regular security checks
options.rationale: ✅ Comprehensive protection blends trust, boundaries, and smart security habits.

options.text: Buy the most expensive security software and never talk about safety
options.rationale: ❌ Software alone cannot replace family communication.

options.text: Leave digital safety entirely up to the school
options.rationale: ❌ Home is the primary place where daily digital habits are formed.

questions.question: Someone calls claiming you won a company raffle and asks for your bank details to deliver the prize. What do you do?
questions.context: Phone scams often use excitement or urgency to trick people.

options.text: Give them my bank details so I do not miss the prize
options.rationale: ❌ Legitimate companies do not ask for sensitive banking credentials to hand out prizes.

options.text: Share the caller's link with friends first
options.rationale: ❌ Never pass along unverified links or offers.

options.text: Hang up and verify independently using the company's official contact number
options.rationale: ✅ Verifying through official channels protects you from phone scams.

options.text: Stay on the line and give them my home address instead
options.rationale: ❌ Sharing personal address details with unverified callers is also risky.

questions.question: Your child is learning programming and technology. How do you encourage them safely?
questions.context: Technical skills grow best alongside strong digital ethics.

options.text: Let them test hacking tools on other people's accounts
options.rationale: ❌ Accessing others' accounts without permission is unethical and illegal.

options.text: Tell them ethics do not matter as long as the code works
options.rationale: ❌ Ethics and safety matter just as much as technical skill.

options.text: Discourage them from learning programming
options.rationale: ❌ Programming is a valuable skill when paired with good guidance.

options.text: Encourage their curiosity while teaching respect for privacy, ethics, and responsible reporting
options.rationale: ✅ Digital ethics are an essential part of learning technology.

questions.question: What is the most important digital safety takeaway to practice every day?
questions.context: Consistent habits turn knowledge into real protection.

options.text: Rely on a password alone and ignore everything else
options.rationale: ❌ Safety requires multiple habits working together.

options.text: Assume everyone online is trustworthy
options.rationale: ❌ Healthy caution is essential online.

options.text: Verify sources, protect personal data, and keep communication open
options.rationale: ✅ Those three habits form the foundation of everyday digital safety.

options.text: Never use the internet for anything
options.rationale: ❌ Safe, mindful use — not avoidance — is the goal.

questions.question: How can you regularly check your family's digital safety readiness?
questions.context: Periodic check-ins keep your family's security habits up to date.

options.text: Never review settings once a phone is set up
options.rationale: ❌ Ongoing review keeps your family protected.

options.text: Check: Are devices updated? Are passwords strong and 2FA on? Do we talk openly?
options.rationale: ✅ A practical checklist helps spot and fix gaps early.

options.text: Check once every few years
options.rationale: ❌ Regular check-ins work best as apps and habits change.

options.text: Assume everything is fine as long as nothing has broken yet
options.rationale: ❌ Security risks often stay hidden until a problem occurs.
